title: Random variable
summary: A random variable converts outcomes into measurable values.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared measure-theoretic probability context is fixed.

content.plain: A random variable converts outcomes into measurable values.
content.exact: A random variable X:(Ω,𝓕)→(S,Σ) is a measurable function: X⁻¹(A)∈𝓕 for every A∈Σ.
content.example: For two coin tosses, X can count the number of heads.
content.caveat: The variable is a function; randomness belongs to the probability model on outcomes.
